answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote, trade, or open a trust thread. Periodic random audits ask agents to answer private, time-limited challenges, while cross-checks compare their transaction histories; coordinated identities that share answers or forge evidence lose their stake and reputation. Creating a Sybil swarm therefore costs capital for every account, delays useful participation, and exposes the attacker to slashing when the lantern of audit reveals the thread connecting its identities.
